title: A Generalized Backward Compatibility Metric

problem.claim: Retraining classifiers with new data can improve overall performance while causing users to encounter incorrect predictions on samples previously predicted correctly by the old classifier.

gap.claim: Existing backward compatibility metrics and methods lack a well-developed theoretical perspective.

contributions.claim: The paper analyzes existing backward compatibility metrics and finds that they essentially assess the same quantity between old and new models.
The paper proposes a generalized backward compatibility metric that can represent existing backward compatibility metrics.
The paper formulates a learning objective based on the generalized metric, derives an estimation error bound, and applies the result to an existing method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that existing backward compatibility metrics are not suitable for imbalanced classification.
The authors report designing an imbalanced-classification backward compatibility metric based on the generalized metric.
The authors empirically demonstrate the practicality of the proposed metric.

narrative_sequence.summary: Classifier retraining with new data is common, but backward compatibility is often not considered.
Improved overall performance can still produce user-confusing errors relative to correct predictions from the old classifier.
Backward compatibility metrics and methods have received interest but lack sufficient theoretical understanding.
The paper analyzes existing metrics, introduces a generalized metric, and derives a learning objective with an estimation error bound.
The analysis addresses imbalanced classification and motivates an empirically evaluated metric for that setting.

source_observation.claim: Existing backward compatibility metrics essentially assess the same quantity between old and new models.

interpretation.claim: Different metrics may provide less conceptual diversity than their names suggest.

application.claim: When comparing related evaluation metrics, first test whether they measure the same underlying quantity before selecting among them.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the metrics may differ in practical behavior or interpretation.

source_observation.claim: Existing backward compatibility metrics are reported as unsuitable for imbalanced classification.

interpretation.claim: Metric suitability can depend materially on the class distribution of the evaluation setting.

application.claim: Evaluate compatibility metrics under the intended data-balance conditions and adapt them when class imbalance changes the measurement.

exception.claim: The abstract does not identify the specific imbalance conditions or failure modes that make the existing metrics unsuitable.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide the mathematical definitions of the metrics.
The abstract does not specify the estimation error bound.
The abstract does not describe datasets, baselines, experimental settings, or numerical results.
